Direction is Term 1 to Term 4 within Grade R, which is the permitted earlier-to-later order; the shared Grade R ancestor and the thin token overlap ('name', 'in') alone were not treated as sufficient, the pair-specific content link was. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (coordinate rank 0) under Skill Area EMERGENT WRITING and Sub-strand 'Emergent Writing:', the first in Term 3 and the second in Term 2. They are substantively complementary emergent-writing capabilities: the second endpoint has the child 'read' their own letters and squiggles as if they carry a message, while the first endpoint has the child distinguish writing from drawing and produce pretend writing mixing copied environmental letters and numerals with squiggles. Producing marks and attributing meaning to those same marks reinforce each other within the same sub-strand, which is pair-specific coherence beyond shared tokens ('letters', 'squiggles') or shared Grade/Skill Area hierarchy. buildsTowards is not supported: the Learning Components of the first (Term 3) endpoint each carry a parallel claim with the Grade R / Term 2 / EMERGENT WRITING / 'Emergent Writing:' ancestor path (83d99627, bd46a3d7, f98c1ea6, b1f1e8a8) from source SFI 0e2d7bb6, showing the Term 3 wording already appears in Term 2 alongside the second endpoint; there is thus no evidenced expansion of capability from the second to the first, only co-occurring complementary skills that CAPS repeats across terms. Symmetric relatesTo with null direction is therefore the correct complete judgment. Evidence limits: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the Grade and Term ancestors are merged banner nodes, so confidence is moderate.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3 Reading and Phonics / Group Guided Reading Skills (rank 3). Source refs place the second SFI in Term 2 ('Uses phonics, context clues and structural analysis decoding skills when reading unfamiliar words') and the first in Term 4 ('Uses phonics, contextual and structural analysis decoding skills and comprehension skills to make meaning'). Within the same grade, direction runs earlier term to later term, so second_to_first. The change is substantive rather than generic repetition: the Term 2 statement applies the decoding toolkit at word level to unfamiliar words, while the Term 4 statement combines those same decoding strategies with comprehension skills for text-level meaning-making, so fluency with the earlier word-attack strategies supports success with the later integrated decoding-plus-comprehension demand. Endpoint evidence is bounded (source evidence truncated for both SFIs; 24 omitted evidence items each), but the retained statement texts and term scope are consistent and sufficient.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills are printed in the same Grade 2 (rank 2), Term 2, 'Reading and Phonics' table, under different sub-strands: 'Daily Phonic Activities of 15 minutes' (Phonics) — 'Reads words from phonics lessons in sentences and other texts' — and 'Paired/Independent Reading' — 'Reads own and others' writing'. They are substantively coherent complementary reading practices: applying decoding and word recognition to connected text, and applying reading to learner-produced text in the same term's daily reading programme. This is meaningful pair-specific coherence rather than generic repetition or mere token overlap ('and', 'reads') or adjacent page indexes. However, no developmental dependency is evidenced: the two bullets are concurrent parallel sub-strand activities in the same Term 2 table (rows 3 and 4 of the same source window), and the target statement shows no expanded capability (more letters, longer texts, greater independence) relative to the source; the supplied LC claim set shows 'reads own and others' writing' recurring as early as Grade R. Same-grade/same-term buildsTowards therefore lacks the required substantive extension evidence, so the symmetric relatesTo decision is used with canonical endpoint order preserved and null direction. Source and LC evidence for both endpoints is truncated and shared ancestors carry merge/audit context, which limits confidence; these warnings are retained rather than resolved.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit under the same Grade R / Term 3 / Listening and Speaking (Oral) / 'Uses visual and pictorial cues to make meaning' sub-strand (same canonical rank 0, same term, so a first-to-second direction is permitted within the grade). The first statement establishes the foundational insight that individual pictures and photographs convey meaning about events, people, places and things, plus oral talk about them (LCs: 'Understands that pictures and photographs convey meaning...', 'Talks about the events, people, places and things conveyed in pictures and photographs'). The second extends this to ordering multiple pictures and constructing and orally relating a connected story (LCs: 'Sequences pictures', 'Relates the story created'), which is a substantive increase in complexity: from single-image meaning-making and description to multi-image sequencing and narrative production. Proficiency in reading meaning from pictures supports success in sequencing them into a coherent told story, so the developmental support runs first to second rather than the reverse. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream merge/audit context, so the judgment rests on the supplied statement texts, shared sub-strand placement and Learning Components.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (rank 0), Listening and Speaking (Oral), sub-strand 'Uses language to investigate and explore', but in different terms: the first is Grade R Term 2 ('Gives explanations and asks for clarification', LCs 'Gives explanations', 'Asks questions for clarification') and the second is Grade R Term 4 ('Asks questions and looks to books, television, computers for explanations', LCs 'Asks questions', 'Looks to books, television, computers for explanations'). This is not mere repeated wording: the Term 4 statement extends oral questioning for clarification beyond the immediate interlocutor to deliberately consulting external information sources (books, television, computers) to obtain explanations, i.e. questioning in service of independent enquiry. Competence in giving explanations and asking clarifying questions orally plausibly supports success in the later, broader enquiry behaviour, so buildsTowards first_to_second. Both endpoints have truncated source and LC evidence and carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests only on the bounded excerpts shown.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit under Grade 1 (rank 1) Reading and Phonics, Sub-strand Phonics (Daily Phonemic Awareness/Phonic Activities). This is not mere repetition: oral phoneme blending/segmenting/substitution is the enabling capability for the Term 2 move to written word building across rime-based word families with a weekly quantity requirement. Within Grade 1, buildsTowards runs from the earlier Term 1 statement to the later Term 2 statement, i.e. second_to_first in the canonical (non-semantic) order. Both endpoints have truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each) and upstream audit/merge context, but the supplied statements, identity scopes and LCs are sufficient and consistent.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit under Grade 1 (rank 1), Term 1, Writing > Handwriting, in the same printed table row (page 63), so the shared hierarchy is context rather than evidence on its own. Direction is first_to_second within the same Grade and same Term, which is permitted. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so no stronger sequencing claim is made.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Emergent Reading Skills (coordinate rank 0, Grade R). The second SFI sits in Term 1 under Sub-strand 'Emergent reading skills' ('Participates in directionality activities such as moving the body left to right and top to bottom'); the first sits in Term 3 under Sub-strand 'Shared Reading' ('‘Reads’ class or group generated texts... sentences written by the teacher while the children are watching, talking and dictating'). Substantively, embodied left-to-right/top-to-bottom directionality is a print-orientation precursor that supports the later emergent 'reading' of teacher-scribed class sentences, where children must track and re-say printed text in the correct order; this is extension from body-level directionality to applying it to connected written text, not mere repeated wording (lexical overlap is only 'and'/'the'). judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R (rank 0), Emergent Reading, sub-strand 'Relates sounds to letters and words', but in different terms: the second ('Understands that words consist of more than one sound. For example, sat - s-a-t done aurally') is anchored to Term 2, while the first ('Recognises aurally and visually some initial consonants and vowels especially at the beginning of common words... points to the h that it says /h/') is anchored to Term 3. Grasping that words are made of discrete sounds plausibly supports isolating and mapping an initial sound to its printed letter, so proficiency in the Term 2 statement supports success with the Term 3 statement. The two statements target different capabilities (fine-motor/spacing conventions vs alphabetic organisation and dictionary skills), and the only lexical overlap flagged by nomination is trivial (shared token 'and', jaccard 0.04) and same-page/same-rank proximity, which cannot establish direction; same-grade/same-term placement supplies no ordering evidence. Hence symmetric relatesTo rather than buildsTowards. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and ancestors carry merge/audit context, so this judgment rests on the bounded printed statements and hierarchy supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade 1 (rank 1, resolved coordinates), Term 2, Skill Area 'Reading and Phonics', but sit under different printed sub-strands: 'Daily Phonemic Awareness/ Phonic Activities' (builds up and breaks down simple single-consonant words into onset and rime, identifying rhymes; LCs tagged blending, segmenting, onset, rime, rhyme) and 'Group Guided Reading' (begins to monitor self when reading, in both word recognition and comprehension; LC tagged self-monitoring, word recognition, comprehension). There is genuine, pair-specific instructional coherence: the onset/rime decoding work is one of the word-level tools a Grade 1 reader draws on when checking and repairing word recognition during guided reading, so the two concurrent Term 2 skills meaningfully reinforce each other within the same skill area. However, the evidence shows no substantive extension, deepening, broadened scope, or increased independence from one statement to the other; they are co-taught in the same term under distinct sub-strands, and the self-monitoring statement also spans comprehension processes beyond phonics. Same-grade, same-term buildsTowards requires substantive developmental evidence, which this bounded evidence does not supply, so the symmetric canonical relatesTo is recorded with no direction. Lexical and structural nomination signals (shared ancestors, rank gap 0, page gap 1, overlap only on function words and fragments) were not treated as semantic support. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R, Listening and Speaking (Oral), sub-strand 'Uses language to investigate and explore' (first: Term 2; second: Term 4), and both are tagged with problem solving ('Solves and completes ten or more piece jig-saw puzzles'; 'Listens to problems and offers solutions' with LCs 'Listens to problems' / 'Offers solutions'). The coherence is a shared problem-solving orientation within one sub-strand, but the capabilities operate in different modalities: the Term 2 item is a hands-on visual-spatial puzzle-completion task, while the Term 4 item is oral comprehension of a stated problem plus verbal proposal of solutions. The evidence shows no expansion of the same capability (no more pieces, longer texts, or greater independence along one skill line), so proficiency with jig-saw puzzles is not shown to support success in oral problem-solving; symmetric conceptual coherence is the supported judgment rather than a forward Term 2 to Term 4 buildsTowards. judgment.rationale: Both Skills share identity scope grade=Grade R | term=Term 3 | skill area=Emergent Reading | sub-strand=Emergent reading skills and are distinct printed bullets from the same table row (row_index=4, window 8, page 49). The first, 'Distinguishes pictures from print: points to a word and asks what the word is' (LC tags: emergent reading, pictures, print, print awareness), and the second, 'Begins to recognise high frequency words used in the classroom: weather words, days of the week, peers' names, months of the year' (LC tags: classroom print, high frequency words, recognising, sight words), are substantively coherent complementary emergent-reading skills: both direct the learner's attention to printed word forms in the classroom/text environment, so they reinforce one another instructionally rather than merely repeating wording. However, they are not the same capability at greater complexity and sit in the same grade and the same term as concurrently listed content, so the bounded evidence does not establish that proficiency in one substantively raises the likelihood of success in the other; a directional buildsTowards would rest on general pedagogical theory rather than pair-specific evidence of expansion. Canonical symmetric relatesTo with null direction is therefore the supported judgment. Limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so shared ancestry, page proximity and LC token overlap were treated as nomination signals only, not as semantic support.
